# The Week Kern County's Safety Net Was Tested From Every Direction

The week of October 18 opened with a boil water notice in Bear Valley Springs and closed with a City Council agenda item about jail beds. In between, Kern County saw a fatal police shooting vigil in south Bakersfield, a wildfire-driven power shutoff that darkened a swath of the county, a pedestrian badly hurt in Oildale, a high school football game stopped by a medical emergency on the sideline, and a series of CHP calls that kept ambulances moving from the county line to the Grapevine.

Public safety, it turns out, is not one story. It is a dozen of them, running at once.

## Power, Water, and the Cost of Prevention

The week's most far-reaching disruption began with wildfire prevention. Public safety power shutoffs left a swath of Kern County without electricity amid wildfire concerns, according to 23ABC. The same week, Bakersfield Now reported that a boil water notice was issued for parts of Bear Valley Springs amid power shutoff issues — a reminder that when the grid goes dark by design, the consequences ripple well past the outage itself.

CAL FIRE listed one active Kern fire during the week: the Cyrus Fire, at 543 acres. The containment figure was not reported in the source material, but the acreage alone places it among the larger incidents of the fall.

Water storage offered its own quiet signal. Isabella Lake stood at 140,906 acre-feet, or 24.8 percent of capacity, with a 30-day trend of minus 22,011 acre-feet. That drawdown is the kind of number that matters less in October than it will in July — but it is the number the county has.

## On the Roads: A Week of Collisions

The California Highway Patrol log for October 17 and 18 reads like a county that never fully sleeps.

In the early hours of October 18, CHP responded to a crash with injuries at 2207 Edison Hwy at 1:55 a.m., and another with injuries at E Panama Ln at S Fairfax Rd at 12:08 a.m. — the same minute as a hit-and-run with no injuries at the SR-99 southbound Woollomes Avenue off-ramp. By 6:54 a.m., there was another hit-and-run, no injuries, at the SR-99 southbound County Line Road on-ramp. At 7:04 a.m., a crash with injuries sent an ambulance to I-5 northbound just north of the No. 4 turn-thru. At 9:11 a.m., a hit-and-run with no injuries was reported at Oildale Drive at Belle Avenue.

The prior day was no lighter. A crash with injuries at SR-99 southbound at SR-119 came in at 12:06 a.m. on October 17. At 9:33 a.m., a hit-and-run with injuries was reported at 2112 Kentucky St. At 11:12 a.m., another hit-and-run, no injuries, at Sterling Road at Hillburn Road. And at 9:57 a.m., CHP logged mud, dirt, or rock on the roadway at the 1600 mile marker of eastbound Highway 178 — the kind of debris call that follows wind and dry hillsides.

Separately, KGET 17 reported that a pedestrian suffered major injuries in an Oildale collision, according to CHP.

## Violence, and the Responses to It

Two shootings at the KBAK television station drew a resolution this week: Bakersfield police arrested a woman in connection with both recent shootings at the station, 23ABC reported.

In south Bakersfield, a vigil was held for a man shot and killed by police. KGET 17 quoted a mourner: "He's in God's arms." The circumstances of the shooting were not detailed in the source material.

Near Olive Drive, a man was charged with attempted murder in a shooting involving a Kern deputy, per KGET 17. And the Kern County Sheriff's Office arrested three people on meth manufacturing, distributing, and gun charges, KGET 17 reported.

Elsewhere in the justice system, a woman accused of vandalizing the Kern County Veterans Memorial was committed to a mental hospital, according to KGET 17.

## The Sideline and the Stands

Friday night football delivered two of the week's most-read stories. Foothill High School forfeited all seven of its wins, 23ABC reported — a decision that reshaped the season's standings in a single stroke.

The same week, the East Bakersfield–Foothill game was stopped due to a medical emergency on the East High sideline, according to KGET 17 and 23ABC. KGET 17 also published Week 9 scores from across Bakersfield and Kern County.

Away from the field, hundreds gathered at Bakersfield's Liberty Bell for a "No Kings" vote-early event ahead of the election, 23ABC reported. And the Via Arté chalk festival transformed a Bakersfield parking lot into a gallery, per 23ABC.

## Enforcement, Immigration, and the Week Ahead

Immigration enforcement produced two distinct stories. A Bakersfield man was detained by ICE on his way to work, and his business partner raised concerns over his treatment, 23ABC reported. Separately, "Rapid Response" volunteers responded to reports of ICE activity under the message "You're not alone," according to 23ABC.

The week ahead is heavy with meetings. The Bakersfield City Council meets Wednesday, October 21, at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. The council is set to discuss possible jail bed space policies, KGET 17 reported. Also on the calendar: a Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meeting and a Historic Preservation Commission meeting, both Tuesday, October 20, at 2 p.m. and 10 a.m. respectively, and a Special Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meeting Tuesday at 2 p.m.

Voters in Bakersfield City Council Ward 7 got a look at their candidates this week: KGET 17 sent a questionnaire and published how they responded.

## The Throughline

Taken one at a time, these are the stories any mid-October week produces. Taken together, they sketch the shape of a county's safety apparatus — the grid operators who cut power to prevent fire, the water district that follows with a boil notice, the CHP dispatchers logging hit-and-runs at midnight, the deputies and officers making arrests, the paramedics called to a football sideline, the council members who will sit down Wednesday to talk about jail beds.

The Cyrus Fire is still burning. Isabella Lake is still dropping. And the week's meetings are already on the calendar.
